newsitem.title: USA: U.S. soldiers' remains recovered from crash site.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soldiers' remains recovered from crash site.

text.p: The Army said Wednesday it recovered the remains of eight paratroopers killed when an Army helicopter crashed and burned on a routine flight at Fort Bragg.
But positive identification of the soldiers had not been completed and their names were not released.
The UH-60L Black Hawk helicopter went down Tuesday afternoon in a wooded area at the southwest corner of the sprawling base, about 20 miles (32 km) west-southwest of Fayetteville, N.C.

The victims were members of the elite 82nd Airborne Division, one of the U.S. military's top battle groups. It was the worst helicopter disaster at Fort Bragg since 1985 when a dozen soldiers were killed in another Black Hawk crash.
At the scene of the crash, 100-foot (30-meter) trees on both sides of the aircraft were scorched to their tops by flames. The ground was blackened for 100 feet (30 meters) around the wreckage.
Chunks of the main rotor blades were scattered in all directions and only the blackened metal hulk of the helicopter's engine remained intact.
In a statement Wednesday, Lt. Gen. Jack Keane, Fort Bragg's commander, said he was "deeply saddened" by the loss.

The paratroopers were taking digital photographs for an upcoming training mission. The cause of the crash had not been determined and would not be known for several weeks, public affairs officer Sgt. Dave Schad said.
